title: Surgical grips: holding the instruments
summary: The scalpel, needle driver and forceps grips a surgical trainee learns first. The gloves read your finger curls and wrist roll only: they cannot see the instrument, the thread, the knot or the tissue. A practice aid, not a qualification.

steps.title: Lesson 1: Scalpel: pencil grip
steps.instruction: Hold the scalpel like a pen between thumb and middle finger, index finger resting on the back of the blade. Ring and little finger curl away.

steps.title: Lesson 2: Scalpel: table-knife grip
steps.instruction: Bring the hand over the handle as you would a dinner knife: index finger on the back of the blade, the handle against the palm.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Needle driver: ring grip
steps.instruction: Thumb and ring finger in the rings, middle finger on top, index finger straight along the shaft. This is the grip for beginners.

steps.title: Lesson 4: Needle driver: palmed grip
steps.instruction: Ring finger through one ring and rest the other on the base of your thumb. It differs from the ring grip by only a little curl, so match the expert closely.

steps.title: Lesson 5: Forceps: pencil grip
steps.instruction: With your other hand, hold the forceps like a pencil between thumb, index and middle finger.
